A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDKA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v1's Appendices A–E to v2 and identifying the added Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original CDKA benchmark results, component and initialization experiments, gradient trajectories, and computational-cost measurements. These are distinguished from baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds Qwen evaluations, image-classification results, fixed-configuration robustness tests, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The summed Kronecker update, component-design principles, initialization, scaling rule, and efficient computation remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 4. The new default-configuration experiment evaluates an existing configuration rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: The GLUE, MetaMathQA/GSM8k, and Code-FeedBack/HumanEval coverage is retained. v2 adds image classification on Stanford Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, RESISC45, SUN397, and SVHN, substantially extending evaluation beyond language to visual domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original NLP tables is unchanged. The new image-classification comparison in Table 13 includes LoRA-Pro and zero-shot CLIP, neither previously reported as an evaluated comparator; LoRA-Pro was already cited in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-3-0.6B, Qwen-3-8B, and LLaMA-3-70B settings, a CLIP image-classification protocol using prompt-based classifiers and test accuracy, and a controlled evaluation fixing the component configuration across models. Section 4 also replaces the explicit single-epoch statement with equal but unspecified epoch counts; this does not establish an actual budget change or rerun.

E4.justification: The original component sweeps, initialization tests, and gradient analysis remain. Section 4.4 adds fixed-configuration robustness testing, while Appendix F adds a component-design-versus-scaling ablation, Qwen and CLIP sensitivity analyses, and fixed-budget design tests on LLaMA-3-70B and CLIP.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results use means and standard deviations over three random seeds, with no stated increase in runs. However, the added CLIP appendix results in Tables 18–20 and 23–24 and LLaMA-3-70B results in Tables 21–22 omit standard deviations, making uncertainty reporting less complete for these analyses.

E6.justification: Tables 2–11 and the computational-cost results are retained unchanged. Newly reported results include Qwen GSM8k scores of 65.83 and 86.56, CLIP average accuracy of 90.08 versus LoRA-One's 89.57, and scaling-only and design-only ablation scores of 49.43 and 55.62. Some new appendix averages are internally inconsistent: the first vision row in Tables 18 and 19 reports 89.69, although its seven listed scores average approximately 87.26.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, alignment theorems, stabilization theorem, and proofs in Appendices B–E retain their substance. v2 adds explanatory notation around Equation 11 and corrects prose typos, without introducing or revising formal results.

C1.justification: The central contributions concerning component design, alignment, and stabilization are retained. The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion extend the empirical claims from NLP to NLP and computer vision, including a new claim of state-of-the-art image-classification performance.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly attributes most performance gains to component design, with stabilization providing an additional benefit. Section 4.4 interprets the fixed-configuration results as evidence of practical transferability, and Section 5 explicitly identifies nonlinear theoretical analysis as an outstanding limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds targeted-layer descriptions and hyperparameter rows for Qwen and CLIP, while retaining the earlier configurations and code-access information. Documentation remains incomplete for the added 70B experiments, and v2 no longer supplies the explicit one-epoch count stated in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the vision datasets, CLIP, Qwen3, and Zhang and Pilanci's LoRA work, and explicitly connects its linear setting to earlier LoRA theory. The related-work discussion and positioning against KronA and MoKA otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, clarifies alignment notation, fixes the NLG results cross-reference from Table 9 to Table 10, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. It adds experimental subsections and Appendix F while preserving the existing narrative organization.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the table presentation with new benchmark, robustness, and ablation tables and an enlarged hyperparameter table. Figure 1's unchanged curves are enlarged and rearranged from side-by-side panels above Table 9 to vertically stacked panels below it; the computational-cost table is relocated and renumbered without changing its results.

improvement.justification: The new vision evaluation and fixed-configuration test substantially strengthen evidence for applicability beyond v1's NLP experiments. Table 17 also directly tests whether gains arise from component design or stabilization, addressing an important attribution gap. These validation gains outweigh localized shortcomings: inconsistent averages in Tables 18–19, missing uncertainty for some appendix results, and less explicit training-budget documentation weaken parts of the added evidence.
